name: Finnish Sign Language
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Rissanen, Terhi (1985), Viittomakielen perusrakenne [The basic structure of Finnish Sign Language], Univ. of Helsinki — sign-language prosody; no online copy located

sources.citation: Jantunen, Tommi (2012). Acceleration peaks and sonority in Finnish Sign Language syllables. In S. Parker (ed.), The Sonority Controversy, 347-382. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton. [author final ms]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Motion-capture study of FinSL syllables; cites Wilbur (1990a) that stressed ASL signs show acceleration changes; no claim about where stress falls in FinSL signs; disyllables analysed for acceleration peaks per syllable, not relative prominence.

sources.citation: Jantunen, Tommi (2011). Foneettisen viittoman ala [The domain of the phonetic sign]. Puhe ja kieli 31:2, 51-65.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only notes (after Blondel & Miller 2001, LSF poetry) that transitional movements can be emphasised (painottaa) like sign movements; in the 'ele' model such emphasis falls on the preparation phase of the sign. Not a lexical stress rule.

sources.citation: Jantunen, Tommi (2008). Katsaus suomalaisen viittomakielen kielitieteelliseen tutkimukseen [Overview of linguistic research on FinSL].
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Research overview: describes Rissanen 1985 as covering lexicon, chereme types (handshape, location, movement) and morphological processes; no FinSL stress/prosody study listed as of 2008.

sources.citation: Jantunen, T; Mesch, J. & Puupponen, A. (2016). Aspects of the rhythm in FinSL and SSL. TISLR12 presentation slides.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Defines rhythm via peaks of prominence at sentence level; nothing on sign-internal stress.

sources.citation: Jantunen, T; Mesch, J; Puupponen, A. & Laaksonen, J. (2016). On the rhythm of head movements in Finnish and Swedish Sign Language sentences. Proc. Speech Prosody 2016, 850-853.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sentence-level head-movement rhythm; no word-stress statement.

sources.citation: Jantunen, Tommi (2015). How long is the sign? Linguistics 53:1, 93-124 (JYX self-archived published version).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Phonetic length of signs vs transitions; no mention of stress.

sources.citation: Jantunen, Tommi (2015). Rinnastuksen prosodiaa suomalaisessa viittomakielessä. XXIX Fonetiikan päivät (Aalto), 15-21.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Prosody of clausal coordination (non-manuals, pauses); silent on lexical stress.

sources.citation: Jantunen, Tommi & Takkinen, Ritva (2010). Syllable structure in sign language phonology. In D. Brentari (ed.), Sign Languages (Cambridge Language Surveys), 312-331. CUP. [author final ms from users.jyu.fi/~tojantun/lataamo/]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Discusses FinSL syllable (movement = syllable, most signs monosyllabic, some disyllables/compounds); stress mentioned only for spoken-language typology (heavy syllables attract stress) and ASL rhythm experiments (Allen, Wilbur & Schick 1991). Nothing on stress placement in FinSL signs.

sources.citation: Jantunen, Tommi (2009 [defended 2008]). Tavu ja lause: tutkimuksia kahden sekventiaalisen perusyksikön olemuksesta suomalaisessa viittomakielessä. Jyväskylä Studies in Humanities 117. Jyväskylä: University of Jyväskylä (summary part, 65 pp.).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No stress-location statement. p.36: quantity-sensitivity in FinSL cannot yet be argued; it should be judged primarily on stress-related prosodic properties, and 'more research is needed, especially on the metrical structure above the syllable level in signed language'. Transcription key uses !…! for an emphasised (painotettu) stretch in sentences (phrase-level emphasis only).

sources.citation: Jantunen, Tommi (2007). Tavu suomalaisessa viittomakielessä. Puhe ja kieli 27:3, 109-126.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Syllable in FinSL (Brentari prosodic model); no mention of paino/stress.
